Baseline `go test ./...` green. Eighteen mutations applied one at a time and reverted; each SURVIVING mutation was re-verified against the FULL `go test ./...`, and the one mutation that only broke the build on an unused import (removing the `slices.Contains` guard) was re-run with the import kept live so the signal is a test result and not a compile error. internal/fsm/* is at 100% statement coverage, so coverage was ignored as evidence throughout.

New source in this shard does carry tests (internal/status/status_test.go, internal/fsm/judge/diffselect_test.go, and the machine/judge/cli tests exercised above); the test gaps recorded below are specific unpinned lines, not a wholesale absence of tests.

findings.note: hardenDiff does not pin the diff path prefixes, so it does not deliver the guarantee its own doc comment states. The comment says it "pins a diff invocation to git's own patch output" so that "the bytes we measure, chunk, hash and lint" are the patch and the review cannot "pass over content nobody saw". --no-ext-diff and --no-textconv close the external-driver and textconv routes, but `diff.noprefix=true` - an ordinary, documented gitconfig setting a developer may well have on - survives both and changes the header shape to `diff --git f.go f.go`. Verified through gitcontext.Collect on a scratch repo: with diff.noprefix set, ctx.Diff's first line is `diff --git f.go f.go`. Every consumer of that payload on this branch keys on the b/ prefix: postImagePathFromHeader (internal/fsm/judge/diffselect.go:70,75) takes the post-image path from the last ` b/` or ` "b/`, so ChangedPaths returns [], DiffHasFile returns false, and ContextFor emits "no diff is available for <file>; it is not among the changed files" followed by an EMPTY changed-paths list. Under the escalation contract added in this same branch (docs/fsm/driving-a-workflow.md), a candidate whose file the diff does not carry becomes unverified_no_evidence and is never judged. The net effect is a run that reports success while judging nothing, silently - precisely the failure mode the comment claims to have closed, reached by a different config knob. `diff.mnemonicPrefix=true` is the same class for the staged and working-tree diffs Collect also gathers (git emits c/ i/ w/ prefixes there). Fix verified at the shell: adding `--src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/` to the same flag list restores a//b/ under diff.noprefix=true, and it costs nothing when the setting is absent.

the pinned set is only --no-ext-diff and --no-textconv; nothing pins src/dst prefixes
strings.LastIndex(rest, " b/") - path extraction requires the b/ prefix and returns "" without it

findings.note: The --no-textconv half of the new guard is load-bearing but completely unpinned: deleting it from the flag list leaves the entire `go test ./...` green. It is not decorative - an empirical probe shows that without it, a repository whose .gitattributes maps *.go to a textconv driver has ctx.Diff replaced by the driver's rendering, with the added code absent from the reviewed payload entirely. The asymmetry is the tell: the sibling threat named in the same comment (an external diff driver, both via gitconfig and via GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF) has two dedicated tests, TestCollectIgnoresExternalDiffDriver and TestCollectIgnoresExternalDiffEnvVar, and removing --no-ext-diff is killed by both. The textconv arm has neither. The reason the existing suite cannot catch it is that branchfiles.go:107 and :129 pass --no-textconv explicitly in their own arg lists, so the BranchFiles tests are insensitive to hardenDiff; the Collect() payload at gitcontext.go:118-173 does NOT pass it and depends on hardenDiff alone. A test in the shape of the two external-diff tests, over Collect rather than over BranchFiles, closes it.

"or a textconv filter" - the comment names the threat the code does not test
"--no-textconv" passed explicitly here, which is why the BranchFiles tests cannot detect its loss from hardenDiff

findings.note: The new KindInfo.NeedsJudge flag is pinned on one of its two assignments and not the other. Setting stillPresentKind's NeedsJudge to false leaves all of `go test ./internal/fsm/...` green; the same mutation on adjudicateKind is killed immediately by TestProductRunAndJudge. NeedsJudge is not cosmetic: machine.needsJudge (machine.go:561) is the predicate machine.go:101 and machine.go:634 use to decide whether Preflight validates judge configuration for a node, and types.go:106 documents exactly that contract. still-present is the sdlc-loop's verify node and is judge-driven (fork exec, statusOut decoded from a judge verdict, Reduce emitting run.BugStatus). With its flag silently lost, an invalid judge model or effort would no longer be caught at Init for a workflow whose verify node is still-present, and would instead fail partway through a run that has already spent calls. This is the duplicated-guard pattern: the field was introduced in this change specifically because "exec: fork does not imply it", and only half of the resulting classification is defended by a test.

findings.note: Three fields of the new machine-readable status contract ship untested. status.go is introduced as "the contract" a host hook branches on, and Blocker's blocking_count, attempt_number and max_attempts are the operator-facing part of it - how many blockers remain and which attempt of how many, which is the escalation signal the CLAUDE.md Completion Rule depends on. Deleting the line that populates all three leaves ./internal/status and ./cmd/... green, and a repository-wide grep finds no assertion on any of the three names outside status.go. The decision surface around them IS well covered (Blocked, the HasUnresolvedBlockers filter and Emit's exit code are each killed by a test), which makes the gap a specific one: what the report DECIDES is pinned, what it REPORTS is not. Every field could ship as zero and the suite would stay green. The rubric treats new source without relevant tests as blocking; one assertion over a populated Blocker closes it.

findings.note: The comment justifying the dropped json.MarshalIndent error misdescribes the type it is reasoning about. It says "Report holds only strings, bools, ints and slices of the same, so marshalling cannot fail; a branch here would be unreachable and untestable." Report holds []reviewlog.Summary, whose RunChain is []runchain.Record, whose Target field is a map[string]string (internal/runchain/runchain.go:41). The conclusion still happens to hold - a map with string keys always marshals, and Go's encoder replaces invalid UTF-8 rather than erroring - but the justification is not a description of this type graph, so the next person who adds a float64 or an `any` to Summary will read a reason that was never actually checking what it claims to check. Restating it as "no field in the graph can produce a marshal error (no floats, no channels, no custom Marshalers)" would make the comment true of the code and would keep working as a review prompt.

findings.note: The status package doc asserts in the present tense that "the hooks are thin shims over it, which is what keeps the enforcement model-agnostic rather than one implementation per host drifting apart". No hooks ship in this repository: there is no hooks directory, and no hook configuration in .claude-plugin, .codex-plugin or .agents. status.Emit's only caller is cmd/metareview/main.go:108. The design intent is sound and the contract is the right shape for it, but the sentence describes an integration that does not exist yet, which is the kind of claim a later reader will act on. Stating it as intent ("a host hook is meant to be a thin shim over it") makes the doc true of the tree.

findings.note: hardenDiff's slices.Contains dedupe guard has no observable behaviour and nothing pins it. Removing it and always appending both flags leaves ./internal/gitcontext and ./internal/contextpack green once the import is kept live so the result is a test outcome rather than an unused-import compile error. Passing --no-textconv twice is harmless to git, so the guard buys nothing except the `slices` dependency and a branch a reader has to reason about; the only call site that would ever trigger it is branchfiles.go:107,129, which pass --no-textconv explicitly. If the dedupe is meant to matter, a test should say why; otherwise the loop is simpler without it.
